officials.name: Paul Ferguson
officials.address: 1425 N. Courthouse Rd., Suite 6700 Arlington, VA 22201
officials.bio: Paul Ferguson was elected to serve as Clerk of the Circuit Court of Arlington County and the City of Falls Church beginning January 1, 2008. He is a 1992 graduate of George Mason Law School. In 2006, Mr. Ferguson was awarded the President’s Award by the Arlington County Bar Association for Outstanding effort, participation, and involvement in the Association.

officials.name: Kim Klingler
officials.bio: Kim E. Klingler was elected Arlington Commissioner of Revenue in November 2023, and took office on January 1, 2024. Before her election, Kim served as the Executive Director for the Columbia Pike Partnership.

officials.name: Parisa Dehghani-Tafti
officials.bio: Parisa Dehghani-Tafti is the Commonwealth’s Attorney for Arlington County and the City of Falls Church, first elected in November 2019 and re-elected in 2023. She brings a twenty-year record of criminal justice reform as an innocence protection attorney, a public defender, and a law professor. Her core philosophy is that safety and justice are complementary values, with a primary responsibility to treat crime as crime and people as people.

officials.name: Mark Schwartz
officials.bio: Mark Schwartz was named County Manager by the Arlington County Board in January 2016 after serving as Acting County Manager the previous six months. He was a Deputy County Manager from October 2010 through June 30, 2015, and was named Acting Deputy County Manager in November 2009. Mark joined County government in December 2005, serving as deputy chief financial officer and later as Director of the Department of Management Finance and Chief Financial Officer before joining the Office of the County Manager.

officials.name: Gretchen Reinemeyer
officials.bio: The Arlington County Electoral Board appointed Gretchen Reinemeyer as General Registrar/Director of Elections for Arlington County in 2019. Gretchen started working in elections as a poll worker in Texas when she was 18. She started her career in public service as an AmeriCorps volunteer with the King County Housing Authority in Seattle.

officials.name: Jose Quiroz
officials.bio: Sheriff Jose Quiroz moved to Arlington with his family when he was 5 years old, and his parents are proud immigrants from Honduras. He served four years in the United States Marine Corps before joining the Arlington County Sheriff’s Office in 2001. In January 2023, he was appointed Sheriff of Arlington County and was elected the 19th Sheriff in November 2023, becoming the first sheriff of Latino descent in Arlington County and Virginia.

officials.name: Ronnie Hassan
officials.office: Director, Department of Cable and Consumer Services

officials.name: Carolyn Campbell
officials.address: 22 Lincoln St. 8th Floor, City Hall Hampton, VA 23669
officials.bio: Carolyn Campbell is a Council member serving her first term from 2025-2028. She holds an associate degree from Virginia Peninsula Community College and a Bachelor of Science from Virginia Tech. Professionally, she is the owner/president of Cornerstone Investors Inc. and previously worked as an assistant vice president/chief engineer.

officials.name: Hope L. Harper
officials.address: 22 Lincoln St. 8th Floor, City Hall Hampton, VA 23669
officials.bio: Hope L. Harper is a Council member serving her second term from 2025-2028, having previously served from 2023-2024. She holds a B.S. from Virginia State University and has worked at Northrop Grumman Corp. since 1998. Harper is also a co-author of 'The Lioness Leads' and is involved in numerous community organizations.

officials.name: Martha Mugler
officials.address: 22 Lincoln St. 8th Floor, City Hall Hampton, VA 23669
officials.bio: Martha Mugler is a Council member serving her first term from January 1, 2023, to December 31, 2026. She holds a B.A. in communications from Radford University and has previously served in the House of Delegates and on the Hampton School Board. Currently, she is a Financial Services Program Manager at Old Point National Bank and has a background in public service and various community affiliations.

officials.name: Randy Bowman
officials.address: 22 Lincoln St. 8th Floor, City Hall Hampton, VA 23669
officials.bio: Randy Bowman is a Council member serving his first term from Jan. 1, 2025 - Dec. 31, 2028. He is the CEO of Bowman's Soul n the Wall and I Scream U Scream, with prior experience in distribution and management at Walmart and Verizon. He is currently pursuing a degree in business management at Norfolk State University.

officials.name: Jimmy Gray
officials.address:
22 Lincoln St.
8th Floor, City Hall
Hampton, VA 23669
officials.bio: Jimmy Gray is currently serving his fourth term as Mayor of Hampton, VA, having previously served as Vice Mayor. He holds an A.A.S. from Tidewater Community College, a B.S. from Hampton University, and a Master of Public Administration from Troy University. Prior to his elected office, he had a distinguished career as Hampton Assistant City Manager and Hampton Fire Chief.

officials.name: Steven L. Brown
officials.address: 22 Lincoln St., 8th Floor, City Hall, Hampton, VA 23669
officials.bio: Steven L. Brown is the Vice Mayor of Hampton, VA, serving his second term from 2023 to 2026. He holds a Bachelor of Arts in Biblical Studies and a Master of Arts in Ministry. He has professional experience with Riverside Health Systems and Calvary Community Church, and is involved with various community organizations.

officials.name: T. Scott Harris
officials.address:
Chenault-Weems Building
7507 Library Drive
Hanover, VA 23069
officials.bio: T. Scott Harris began his career in county government in 1986 and was elected Commissioner of the Revenue in 1999. Since then, he has focused on improving department functions through efficiency, accuracy, and enhanced customer service. He holds a Master's Degree in Public Administration and is a Master Commissioner of the Revenue.

officials.name: Phillip Jones
officials.address: 2400 Washington Ave. - 10th Floor Newport News, VA 23607
officials.bio: Phillip Jones is the 27th Mayor of Newport News, Virginia, and the city’s youngest elected mayor, focused on strengthening education, enhancing public safety, and bringing innovation to City Hall. A graduate of the U.S. Naval Academy with an MBA and MPP from Harvard, he served as a Marine Corps infantry officer and advised Fortune 500 companies as a consultant.

officials.name: Carlos J. Clanton
officials.bio: Carlos Clanton was elected to the Norfolk City Council beginning January 1, 2025, to represent the residents of Superward 7. A proud native son of Norfolk, he was raised in the Lambert's Point and Park Place communities, developing a strong sense of leadership and a deep understanding of resilience. His lifelong commitment to being a catalyst for positive change has made him a trusted and respected voice for residents across the city.

officials.name: Courtney R. Doyle
officials.bio: Courtney R. Doyle was elected to Norfolk City Council on May 1, 2018, representing Ward 2. She also serves as Vice President of Marketing for Sentara Health and is actively involved in various civic organizations and task forces. Ms. Doyle holds a Bachelor's degree from the University of Maryland and an MBA from Old Dominion University.

officials.name: Jeremy D. McGee
officials.bio: Jeremy D. McGee was elected to represent Superward 6 on November 5, 2024. Mr. McGee is the President and CEO of Radiant Digital, a nationwide digital media company. Together with his wife Malia, Jeremy has founded several Norfolk-based businesses in the residential and commercial real estate sector.

officials.name: John E. "JP" Paige
officials.bio: John E. “JP” Paige was elected to serve on Norfolk City Council on November 8th, 2022, to represent Ward 4. Councilman Paige's lifelong passion to uplift Norfolk’s underserved communities was the catalyst for his decision to serve in this capacity. As an entrepreneur and accomplished speaker, Mr. Paige consistently advocates the importance of community contribution though determination, personal responsibility, and accountability.

officials.name: Mamie B. Johnson
officials.bio: Mamie B. Johnson was elected to Norfolk City Council on May 6, 2014, to represent Ward 3. She is a career educator, having served as a teacher and instructional specialist for Norfolk Public Schools and Virginia Beach Public Schools. Ms. Johnson is also a member of several boards and organizations, including Virginia First Cities Coalition and the National Black Caucus of Local Elected Officials.

officials.name: Thomas R. Smigiel Jr
officials.bio: Thomas "Tommy" R. Smigiel Jr. was elected to City Council in 2010 and represents Ward 5. He is the principal of Granby High School and was recognized as the 2008 Virginia Teacher of the Year. He co-chairs the East Little Creek Road Advisory Committee and the Mayor’s Ocean View Advisory Committee, and served as the 100th President of the Virginia Municipal League.

officials.name: Kenneth Cooper Alexander, Ph.D.
officials.bio: Kenneth Cooper Alexander was elected Mayor of the City of Norfolk on May 3, 2016, and re-elected in May 2020 and November 2024. He is a lifelong resident of Norfolk and has distinguished himself through his civic, business, legislative, and community leadership. Dr. Alexander is president of Metropolitan Funeral Service, and Vice Chancellor for Strategic Partnerships of Virginia Community College System (VCCS).

officials.name: Martin A. Thomas Jr
officials.bio: Martin A. Thomas Jr. was elected to represent Ward 1 on August 23, 2016 and was elected Vice Mayor in July 2018. Mr. Thomas is a partner at the Decker Law Firm in downtown Norfolk where he has litigated personal injury cases since 2006. He resides with his wife, Maggie, and their two sons in the Wards Corner area of Norfolk.

officials.name: Joseph L. Cobb
officials.address: Noel C. Taylor Municipal Building 215 Church Avenue Roanoke, VA 24011
officials.bio: Joseph L. Cobb has served as Chaplain at Hermitage Roanoke and as Outreach Coordinator for Highland Park Elementary School. He previously pastored Metropolitan Community Church of the Blue Ridge and was Executive Director for Interfaith Hospitality Network. He holds an M.S. in Divinity from Perkins School of Theology and a B.S. in Philosophy from Southwestern College.

officials.bio: Operations Consultant, Carilion Clinic, Specializing in Operational Efficiency. Former Community Outreach Liaison for Delegate Sam Rasoul. He holds a Bachelor of Science in Community Health from George Mason University and is pursuing a Master of Science in Population Health Science from the University of Alabama.

officials.name: S. Terry McGuire
officials.address: Noel C. Taylor Municipal Building 215 Church Avenue Roanoke, VA 24011
officials.bio: S. Terry McGuire serves as an Instructional Assistant for Roanoke City Public Schools. Her professional background includes roles as a Senior Legislative Representative for Earthjustice, Washington Representative for the Sierra Club, and Field Organizer for various human rights and conservation organizations. She holds a B.S. in Environmental Policy & Planning from Virginia Tech.

officials.name: Vivian Sanchez-Jones
officials.address: Noel C. Taylor Municipal Building 215 Church Avenue Roanoke, VA 24011

officials.name: Ebony Wright
officials.bio: Council Member Ebony Wright was elected to the Suffolk City Council on November 5, 2024, representing the Sleepy Hole Borough. A Suffolk resident since 2000, she served in the U.S. Navy and held key positions in the Departments of Justice and Defense, specializing in legal and legislative affairs. She is also the founder and president of a nonprofit organization that provides scholarships to Suffolk Public Schools students.

officials.name: John Rector
officials.bio: Council Member John T. Rector was elected to the Suffolk City Council in November of 2022 and sworn in on January 3, 2023, as the representative of the Suffolk Borough. His term expires on December 31, 2026. A resident of the City of Suffolk for over 35 years, Council Member Rector is currently a Realtor with Chorey and Associates Realty, LTD.

officials.name: LeOtis Williams
officials.bio: Council Member LeOtis Williams was elected to the Suffolk City Council from the Whaleyville Borough in November of 2020. His term expires on December 31, 2028. Council Member Williams is a self-made entrepreneur as the owner of businesses in the City of Suffolk.

officials.name: Shelley Butler Barlow
officials.bio: Council Member Shelley S. Butler Barlow was appointed to the Suffolk City Council in February 2021, representing the Chuckatuck Borough, and was elected for a full term in 2022. A long-time Suffolk resident, she farms with her husband at Cotton Plains Farm and has nearly 40 years of experience in agriculture. She is actively involved in various community groups and served on the Virginia Department of Agriculture and Consumer Services Board of Directors.

officials.name: Timothy Johnson
officials.bio: Council Member Timothy Jett "Tim" Johnson was born in 1955 in Suffolk, Virginia, and earned a Bachelor of Science degree in Ornamental Horticulture from Virginia Polytechnic Institute in 1978. He owns and operates Johnson's Gardens Inc., and has been involved with the Suffolk Lions Club, Paul D. Camp Community College, Nansemond-Suffolk Academy Boards, Boy Scouts of America, and the Suffolk Community Gardens Project. He was elected to the Suffolk City Council in November 2014, representing the Holy Neck Borough, and his term expires on December 31, 2026.

officials.name: Michael Duman
officials.bio: Mayor Michael D. “Mike” Duman was elected to the Suffolk City Council on November 2, 2010, and was sworn in on January 3, 2011, as the representative for the Chuckatuck Borough. He was reelected in November 2014 and November 2018. He was elected Mayor in November 2020 and reelected in November 2024 for an additional term.

officials.name: Lue Ward
officials.bio: Vice Mayor Lue R. Ward, Jr. was born in the former Nansemond County, Virginia. He was elected to the Suffolk City Council on November 6, 2012 and was sworn in on January 2, 2013, as the representative of the Nansemond Borough. He was elected by his colleagues as Vice Mayor on January 3, 2023. Vice Mayor Ward's term expires December 31, 2028.

officials.name: Ebony Wright
officials.bio: Ebony Wright was elected to the Suffolk City Council on November 5, 2024, representing the Sleepy Hole Borough. A committed public servant and community leader, she served in the U.S. Navy and held key positions in federal service, specializing in legal and legislative affairs. She also founded a nonprofit providing scholarships to students in Suffolk Public Schools.

officials.name: John Rector
officials.bio: Council Member John T. Rector was elected to the Suffolk City Council in November of 2022 and sworn in on January 3, 2023, as the representative of the Suffolk Borough. His term expires on December 31, 2026. A resident of the City of Suffolk for over 35 years, Council Member Rector is currently a Realtor with Chorey and Associates Realty, LTD.

officials.name: LeOtis Williams
officials.bio: Council Member LeOtis Williams was elected to the Suffolk City Council from the Whaleyville Borough in November of 2020. His term expires on December 31, 2028. Council Member Williams is a self-made entrepreneur as the owner of businesses in the City of Suffolk.

officials.name: Shelley Butler Barlow
officials.bio: Council Member Shelley S. Butler Barlow was appointed to the Suffolk City Council in February 2021, representing the Chuckatuck Borough, and was elected for a full term in 2022. A long-time Suffolk resident, she farms with her husband at Cotton Plains Farm and has nearly 40 years of experience in agriculture. She is actively involved in various community groups and served on the Virginia Department of Agriculture and Consumer Services Board of Directors.

officials.name: Timothy Johnson
officials.bio: Council Member Timothy Jett "Tim" Johnson was born in 1955 in Suffolk, Virginia, and earned a Bachelor of Science degree in Ornamental Horticulture from Virginia Polytechnic Institute in 1978. He owns and operates Johnson's Gardens Inc., and has been involved with the Suffolk Lions Club, Paul D. Camp Community College, Nansemond-Suffolk Academy Boards, Boy Scouts of America, and the Suffolk Community Gardens Project. He was elected to the Suffolk City Council in November 2014, representing the Holy Neck Borough, and his term expires on December 31, 2026.

officials.name: Michael Duman
officials.bio: Mayor Michael D. Duman was first elected to the Suffolk City Council in 2010, representing the Chuckatuck Borough, and was subsequently reelected. He was elected Mayor in November 2020 and reelected in 2024. Mayor Duman is a graduate of Old Dominion University and served as a commissioned officer in the United States Army Reserve.

officials.name: Lue Ward
officials.bio: Vice Mayor Lue R. Ward, Jr. was born in the former Nansemond County, Virginia. He was elected to the Suffolk City Council on November 6, 2012 and was sworn in on January 2, 2013, as the representative of the Nansemond Borough. He was elected by his colleagues as Vice Mayor on January 3, 2023. Vice Mayor Ward's term expires December 31, 2028.
